# Independent audit: all three homothetic fibers

Audited source: three-homothetic-fibers-all-ratios-and-translations.md.

Mathematical verdict: **PASS**. The proof establishes the stated scoped three-fiber theorem in every \(d\ge2\), with arbitrary positive homothety ratios and translations. Dimension one is correctly separated and referred to the previously independently audited exact interval theorem. It does not establish unrestricted OC.

The standard-library verifier supporting computation verify_three_homothetic_all_ratios.py independently reruns successfully: 3534 exact scalar checks, 721 compatible radius cases, 6400 actual translated-triangle oblique caps, and vertical caps. Its excluded-dimension diagnostic uses \(d=1,t=2/5\), where the proposed scalar extension is strictly false. These checks supplement the full proof audited below.

## 1. Normalization and complete case split

The base reflection interchanges the endpoint radii without changing the middle. The subsequent continuous shear fixes the integer base, has fiber Jacobian one, and sends the middle and larger endpoint to \(RK\) and \(sK\), respectively. The remaining endpoint translation is exactly \(a+c-2b\).

The midpoint inclusion gives \(2R\ge r+s\) before its support-function cancellation is used. Hence the cancellation has the valid nonnegative coefficient
\[
a'\in(2R-r-s)K.
\]
It gives \(A\subseteq(2R-s)K\). The latter radius is at least \(r>0\). Thus \(R\le s\) really yields the nested chain \(A\subseteq RK\subseteq sK\), despite the arbitrary initial translations.

After the ordinary heavy-fiber cases, the only remaining ordering is \(r\le s<R\) with \(R^d<r^d+s^d\). The displayed increasing-in-\(s\) power difference proves \(R-s<r/2\) for every integer \(d\ge2\). No implicit smallness assumption is added.

## 2. Actual retained endpoint and scalar inequality

Writing \(\varepsilon=R-s\), the retained copy
\[
A_0=a'+(r-2\varepsilon)K
\]
is full-dimensional and contained in the original endpoint \(A\). The support cancellation places its translation in \((s+2\varepsilon-r)K\); adding the retained radius gives exactly \(s\). This proves \(A_0\subseteq sK\) with its actual translation intact. Its centroid need not be zero, which is permitted by the measurable-subset theorem being used.

The scalar statement
\[
(r-2\varepsilon)^d\ge
\tfrac12\bigl[r^d+s^d-(s+\varepsilon)^d\bigr]
\]
is valid on the stated full parameter range. After normalization, increasing \(\lambda=s/r\) can only increase \((\lambda+t)^d-\lambda^d\), so the worst case is \(\lambda=1\). The function
\[
2(1-2t)^d+(1+t)^d
\]
is convex and has its unique interior minimum at
\(t=(1-k)/(2+k)\), \(k^{d-1}=1/4\). Its minimum is exactly
\[
\frac{3^d}{2(2+k)^{d-1}}.
\]
Jensen applied to \(x^{d-1}\) at \(1,1,k\) gives
\[
((2+k)/3)^{d-1}\le(2+k^{d-1})/3=3/4,
\]
which makes that minimum at least two. The equality \(d=2\), \(s=r\), \(\varepsilon=r/3\) has a positive right-hand bracket and proves that the universal coefficient \(1/2\) cannot be increased. The strictness for \(d>2\) is correctly stated.

The passage from \(1/2\) to \(\Gamma_d\) is made only where the bracket is positive, namely the nonheavy strip. This direction would require qualification outside that strip; the saved text provides it.

## 3. The same actual middle centroid and no double counting

The earlier subset theorem counts \(A_0,sK,sK\) at the actual middle centroid zero. Its middle term is only the \(sK\) copy. The uncounted middle portion is computed at this exact same point:
\[
|RK\cap H|-|sK\cap H|
=(R^d-s^d)|K\cap H|,
\]
where \(H\) is the through-zero continuous halfspace. Both copies are concentric, and one is contained in the other. Thus adding the difference is legitimate and pays precisely the new middle contribution; no generic depth claim for a displaced added shell is used.

This proves the stronger strip lower bound
\[
\Gamma_dR^dV+\tfrac12(r-2\varepsilon)^dV.
\]
The scalar estimate converts it into the required total-source target. Subtracting that target gives the recorded positive surplus
\[
\frac{1-2\Gamma_d}{4}
V(r^d+s^d-R^d).
\]

Purely base-normal caps contain the entire middle fiber and one entire endpoint. These masses exceed the same displayed lower bound. Moving merely containing caps parallel to their through-candidate caps preserves the required inequality. Closed supporting boundaries are null in every positive full-dimensional fiber; vertical boundary fibers are counted in full.

## 4. Other cases, candidates, and scope

When \(R\le s\), the same subset theorem counts \(A,RK,RK\) and the nonheavy inequality \(s^d<R^d+r^d\) gives the required target. If that inequality fails, the largest endpoint is heavy and its own centroid works. The heavy middle case is handled independently. This proves the deterministic rule: use a heavy fiber's centroid when available; otherwise use the actual middle centroid.

No argument requires the original centroids to be affine in the integer base, or the common body to be symmetric. Every selected point belongs to an actual positive fiber. Extra zero-volume integer fibers do not change the full-\(d\)-dimensional mixed measure, and none is used as a source. The theorem counts exactly the three specified positive fibers.

The role of middle homothety is essential in the cap-difference identity above. The saved source correctly declines an arbitrary-middle-body conclusion.

No mathematical correction is required.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
